title: أَنْ against إِلَى, the Irregular رَأَى، يَرَى, the Four Seasons, and How أَنْ Drops the نُون
summary: Drilling lesson seventeen, the class sorts out a confusion worth having: both أَنْ and إِلَى can be rendered to in English, but إِلَى points to a place or direction while أَنْ attaches to an action — أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ is I want to eat, not I want towards eating. The session also works through مُنْذُ, the irregular رَأَى، يَرَى, and the names of the four seasons, and closes on a rule for the next lesson: where a verb already ends in a نُون, أَنْ drops that نُون instead of adding a fatḥa.
key_points: أَنْ and إِلَى both translate as to, but differently: إِلَى marks a direction or place — ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ — while أَنْ introduces an action, as in أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ, I want to eat.

لَام التَّعْلِيل is used only when giving the reason for something; where the sense is merely wanting to do something, أَنْ is the correct choice. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ against خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ.

Turning a first-person statement into the third person means changing every pronoun and verb with it: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ … مَقْعَدِي بَعِيدٌ عَنْكَ … لَا أَرَى becomes يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ … لِأَنَّ مَقْعَدَهُ بَعِيدٌ عَنْهُ … لَا يَرَى.
قَدْ has no meaning of its own beyond emphasising that something has already happened — قَدْ دَرَسْتُ, I have already studied — and the لَام adds further emphasis still.
مُنْذُ (since) is a حَرْف الجَرّ, so what follows takes a kasra: مُنْذُ أُسْبُوعٍ، مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ، مُنْذُ خَمْسِ سَنَوَاتٍ.
رَأَى، يَرَى is irregular: the form would have been يَرْأَى, but the medial hamza was dropped for ease, giving يَرَى، تَرَى، أَرَى، نَرَى.
أَخَذَ in the first person becomes آخُذُ, the two hamzas merging just as in آكُلُ.
فُصُول are the seasons, and the four are الشِّتَاء (winter), الرَّبِيع (spring), الصَّيْف (summer), and الْخَرِيف (autumn).

Where a مُضَارِع verb already ends in a نُون — تُرِيدُونَ، يَخْرُجُونَ — أَنْ cannot add a fatḥa, since the ending is already fixed. Instead it drops the نُون: تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَذْهَبُوا، يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا. The same happens with the feminine forms.
أَنْ belongs to the حُرُوف النَّاصِبَة, the particles that put the following verb into the accusative, which is why it is also called أَنْ النَّاصِبَة.
حَمَّام strictly means the place where one bathes — hence the Turkish bathhouses — while مِرْحَاض is specifically the toilet, though colloquial Arabic now uses حَمَّام for both.
الْعَشَاء is dinner and الْغَدَاء is lunch; the Arabs' saying الْعَشَاء قَبْلَ الْعِشَاء works because both words share a root, dinner being eaten around that time.

Vocabulary: ضَجَّة and ضَوْضَاء (noise), سَبَب (reason, as in Urdu), بَصَقَ، يَبْصُقُ (to spit), مِفْتَاح with its plural مَفَاتِيح (keys), ظَرْف (an envelope, or any container), إِعْلَان (announcement), and عِلَاج (medical treatment).
questions: [00:02:01] Q: Doesn't أَنْ mean to, the same as إِلَى? — A: Both can be rendered to, but إِلَى is directional — he went to the masjid — whereas أَنْ introduces an action, as in I want to eat. You are not travelling toward a place called eating.
[00:03:00] Q: I did not follow when أَنْ was first introduced. — A: It is picked up with exposure and context; it had appeared several times before being named.
[00:12:00] Q: What does قَدْ mean? — A: It has no specific meaning of its own; it emphasises that something has already taken place, and the لَام emphasises further.

[00:15:06] Q: What is the difference between حَمَّام and مِرْحَاض? — A: حَمَّام is properly the bathing place, as in the Turkish bathhouses; مِرْحَاض is the toilet itself. Colloquially حَمَّام now covers both.
[00:17:00] Q: Why does the object not change its ending there? — A: Because of the attached يَاء — the pronoun does not change, so the word stays as it is.
[00:23:00] Q: Where does نَسِيتُ occur in the Qur'ān? — A: In Sūrat al-Kahf — فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ — and also in Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام's request to Khiḍr, لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ.
[00:36:00] Q: Why is it يَرَى and not يَرْأَى? — A: The medial hamza was dropped because the full form is difficult to pronounce, giving يَرَى، تَرَى، أَرَى، نَرَى.
[00:38:00] Q: Do the Arabs have all four seasons? — A: They do, and الشِّتَاء and الصَّيْف both appear in the Qur'ān, while الرَّبِيع and الْخَرِيف appear in the aḥādīth.
[00:43:00] Q: What happens when أَنْ meets a verb that already ends in a نُون? — A: It cannot add a fatḥa to an ending already set, so it drops the نُون instead: تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَذْهَبُوا.

quiz.q: What is the difference between أَنْ and إِلَى when both translate as to?
options: إِلَى marks a direction or place; أَنْ introduces an action
إِلَى is for the future; أَنْ is for the past
أَنْ is only used in questions
quiz.a: ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ is directional; أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ concerns the action of eating.

quiz.q: Which is correct for Hāshim wants to go to Egypt?
options: يُرِيدُ هَاشِمٌ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى مِصْرَ
يُرِيدُ هَاشِمٌ أَنَّ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى مِصْرَ
quiz.a: The lām is only for giving a reason; plain wanting to do something takes أَنْ, and the destination then takes إِلَى.

quiz.q: What does قَدْ contribute to قَدْ دَرَسْتُ?
options: It emphasises that the action has already happened
quiz.a: It carries no independent meaning beyond stressing the pastness — I have already studied.

quiz.q: What kind of word is مُنْذُ?
quiz.a: مُنْذُ أُسْبُوعٍ، مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ — the following noun takes a kasra.

quiz.q: Why is the present tense of رَأَى simply يَرَى?
options: Because it is a doubled verb
Because the medial hamza of يَرْأَى was dropped for ease of pronunciation
Because it has only two root letters
quiz.a: The expected يَرْأَى was awkward, so the hamza went — giving يَرَى، تَرَى، أَرَى، نَرَى.
الشِّتَاء winter, الرَّبِيع spring, الصَّيْف summer, الْخَرِيف autumn — the season the class was in at the time.

quiz.q: What does أَنْ do to a verb that already ends in a نُون, such as تَذْهَبُونَ?
quiz.a: There is no room for a fatḥa, so the نُون falls away — يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا.

options: Particles that put the following verb into the accusative
Particles that make a verb past tense
quiz.a: أَنْ is one of them, which is why it is also called أَنْ النَّاصِبَة.

quiz.q: What strictly distinguishes مِرْحَاض from حَمَّام?
options: مِرْحَاض is the toilet; حَمَّام is properly the bathing place
حَمَّام is the toilet; مِرْحَاض is the sink
مِرْحَاض is a public facility only
quiz.a: Hence the Turkish bathhouses called ḥammām; colloquial Arabic now uses حَمَّام for both.
الْغَدَاء is lunch, as against الْعَشَاء for dinner — the latter sharing a root with الْعِشَاء.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ
quran_examples.transliteration: innahu yarākum huwa wa-qabīluhu min ḥaythu lā tarawnahum
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the irregular رَأَى، يَرَى, giving both يَرَاكُمْ and تَرَوْنَهُمْ in one āyah; it speaks of Shayṭān and his kind.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا ۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla lā takhāfā, innanī maʿakumā asmaʿu wa-arā
quran_examples.translation: He said: Do not fear. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.
quran_examples.note: Spoken to Mūsā and Hārūn عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام. It carries أَرَى from the same irregular verb, the dual prohibition لَا تَخَافَا from the نَهْي chart, and إِنَّنِي from the earlier lesson.

quran_examples.arabic: فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-innī nasītu al-ḥūta wa-mā ansānīhu illā al-shayṭān
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan.
quran_examples.note: A student's answer for نَسِيتُ, which came up again in the exercises on forgetting to do something.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِي مِنْ أَمْرِي عُسْرًا
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla lā tuʾākhidhnī bi-mā nasītu wa-lā turhiqnī min amrī ʿusrā
quran_examples.translation: He said: Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not cover me in difficulty.
quran_examples.note: The second place the teacher cited for نَسِيتُ, spoken by Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام to Khiḍr; بِمَا here is مَا الْمَوْصُولَة, and both clauses are prohibitions.

quran_examples.translation: The journey of winter and summer.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's answer to whether the seasons appear in the Qur'ān: two of the four are named here, الشِّتَاء and الصَّيْف.

quran_examples.arabic: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا
quran_examples.transliteration: yurīdūna an yakhrujū mina al-nāri wa-mā hum bi-khārijīna minhā
quran_examples.translation: They will wish to come out of the Fire, but they will never come out of it.
quran_examples.note: The example the teacher used for the coming rule: the plural would be يَخْرُجُونَ, but after أَنْ the نُون is dropped to give يَخْرُجُوا. The second clause also shows مَا negating with the بَاء on its خَبَر.
